entities.summary: Regnaud de La Porte (Raynaud) was a French bishop and Cardinal, born in Allassac, who played a pivotal role in the medieval Catholic Church. He served as bishop of Albi from 1295 until his death in 1325, during which time he worked tirelessly to promote the interests of the Church and its flock. Regnaud's legacy can be seen in the numerous foundations and charitable institutions he established, including the Hospital of Saint-Jean de Saverne, which provided care and shelter to the poor and marginalized. Despite his significant contributions to the Church, Regnaud's personal life and relationships remain somewhat of a mystery, with some accounts suggesting he was known for his strict adherence to the Church's moral code. As a cardinal, Regnaud participated in several high-profile conclaves, including that of 1294, which elected Pope Celestine V. He also played a key role in the construction of several important cathedrals, including that of Sainte-Geneviève in Paris. Regnaud's influence can be seen in the numerous artists, writers, and thinkers who sought his counsel and approval, including the famous poet and philosopher, Guillaume de Machaut. Regnaud's impact on Western culture is undeniable, with his legacy continuing to inspire and influence artists, writers, and scholars to this day.
